about: This template is a hand-drawn bar chart under the wobbly, underlined title "What Gives People Feelings of Power". The first two bars are labeled Money and Status and are fairly short; the third bar, painted pink, stretches almost across the page but has no label. That blank label is the whole template: whatever you write there is being declared a bigger source of power than wealth or social rank. The humor comes from filling it with something tiny and petty, like getting the last slice of pizza or having your phone at 100 percent, so the chart treats a trivial victory with the seriousness of a survey result.
origin: The chart started as a webcomic by the Instagram cartoonist iamnotanartist_ in 2019. People quickly cropped out the original answer and began writing their own label next to the longest bar.
usage:
There is one text box, sitting to the left of the long pink bar. Write the small, oddly specific thing that makes you feel unstoppable. Because Money and Status are already printed above it, the joke is the gap between those two serious answers and your trivial one.

Short, concrete moments work best: a feeling everyone recognizes but nobody would admit is their main source of confidence. Specific details (the exact app, the exact chore, the exact number) make it funnier than a vague label.
ideas: the build passing on the first try
finding the TV remote before anyone else
leaving the group chat on read
knowing the wifi password at a party
hitting a 3-pointer in an empty gym
aka: What Gives People Feelings of Power
